script.base: Buffalo is a 15.5-point home favorite with a 32.0 implied total, so the book expects a lead by halftime and a second-half clock kill. James Cook (53 carries, 284 yards in three games) and Josh Allen (20 carries, 120 yards) carry the run; New Orleans, implied 16.5, falls behind and Spencer Rattler throws, with Chris Olave (37 targets) and Juwan Johnson (28 targets) as the chase options. Spread 15.5 is a blowout flag, so Buffalo starter snaps late are not safe.
script.flip1: New Orleans hangs around, Buffalo cannot just run, Allen stays in the pass game to Kincaid, Shakir, Coleman and Palmer, and Alvin Kamara keeps early-down carries against a Buffalo run defense allowing 6.24 YPC.
script.flip2: Buffalo is up big by the middle of the third, Cook and the starting receivers sit, Ray Davis (10 carries, 26 yards, one game of 24) mops up, and New Orleans either inflates Olave, Johnson and Shaheed in garbage time or stalls after three-and-outs.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse injury report, before inactives: BUF LB Matt Milano Out (pectoral) vacates the coverage linebacker spot, which helps tight ends, backs and slots, so Juwan Johnson and Kamara's receiving role gain; the backup LB is not named. BUF DT Ed Oliver Out (ankle) softens the interior, a plus for Kamara/Miller efficiency and a minus for interior pressure on Rattler. BUF DE A.J. Epenesa Questionable (pectoral) and BUF T Spencer Brown Questionable (calf) are unresolved; if Brown sits, Buffalo rushing efficiency and pass protection worsen. Final inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: Not charted. No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone rate in the pack. Location proxy only: BUF allows YPA left 5.18 on 28 attempts, middle 8.91 on 11, right 5.42 on 36. NO allows left 5.66 on 38, middle 12.11 on 18, right 7.56 on 32.
matchup.pressure: BUF blitz rate 33 percent; NO EPA per dropback is +0.11 versus blitz and -0.09 versus no blitz, so New Orleans has been better when blitzed. NO blitz rate 31 percent; BUF EPA per dropback is +0.54 versus blitz and +0.28 versus no blitz. Chase Young out reduces the edge rush Allen sees; Epenesa is only questionable; Oliver out weakens Buffalo's interior.
matchup.bleeds: Buffalo bleeds the run: 6.24 YPC allowed and 18 runs of 10-plus, with only 5 passes of 20-plus for 81 yards. New Orleans is the opposite: 3.83 rush YPC and 9 runs of 10-plus, but the middle (12.11 YPA) and explosives (8 passes of 20-plus for 96 yards) bleed.
matchup.overlap: Johnson (28 targets, 176 yards, 177 air yards, about 6.3 yards per target) overlaps the vacated Milano spot and Buffalo's small-sample middle, not the deep game Buffalo has suppressed. Olave (311 air yards, only 165 receiving) and Shaheed (203 air yards) need explosives Buffalo has not given up. Cook's carry share overlaps a strong NO run defense (3.83 YPC), not a weak one. Kincaid and Shakir overlap NO's middle bleed, but a 32-point clock-kill cuts their volume, and Chase Young being out makes a Buffalo receiver under a bad fade.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and this lost because the counter-case was the game. Buffalo handed Cook 24 carries, the 3.83 YPC was three soft rushing opponents, Allen did not need designed runs, and Cook cleared 108.5 the way he did in the 132-yard game, with 108 already only a half-yard under the number. Johnson saw a full target share and still finished 49 or 51 because the backup linebacker was fine and Buffalo's low explosive rate sat on the intermediate, while New Orleans' few points came on the ground against a 6.24 YPC defense missing Ed Oliver. The shared kill is an early Kamara efficiency script that keeps NO close enough to cap Johnson's chase volume and still lets Cook grind.
slip_story: One story, not a shootout and not an under-plus-overs mix: Buffalo leads and the clock tilts run, but NO's run defense and Allen's rush share cap Cook under 108.5, while the dog throws and Milano's absence are the path for Johnson over 51.5. Cook is script-dependent on efficiency. No third leg, because every Buffalo receiver under fights NO's middle and explosive bleed and Chase Young being out, and Kamara's rush number is a cancel between a bad script and a 6.24 YPC defense.
